reviews.text:
It was my first visit.
On this day, Chef Meditation Ha was in charge.

1. The objects are very stylish and pretty (S-shaped die, cat or dog chopstick rest, fish-patterned glass, etc...)

2. Careful consideration and detail in cleaning the plate for each piece.

3. Shari is excellent in both texture and release, and the vinegar scent is light and pleasantly spreads before disappearing cleanly. The salting is not strong and there is no sweetness.

4. Excellent customer service from Chef Seong-ha, who jokes around a lot and explains things well.

5. Compared to the Spanish farmed tuna that is used in this price range, which is overly oily and has a weak fleshy and acidic taste, this tuna is not too oily and has a good acidity and fleshy taste.

6. White fish is also ripened well, so it retains its sweetness and lightness.

7. Hikarimono is also good. In particular, the herring is clean and oily, and goes well with the auxiliary ingredients (chives, shiso, sudachi juice), giving a refreshing nuance.

All the food is just right to a pleasant level without being excessive.

A business that doesn't seem to have much to do with likes and dislikes

This personality is reflected in the taste as well as the clean, meticulous, and tasteful interior.

reviews.text: Sakaba Ondo is a restaurant in Apgujeong Rodeo Station where you can enjoy dishes and alcohol prepared by a seafood sommelier.​The 59-degree course menu was great to enjoy at your leisure while on a date. Thanks to the care put into each dish, I was amazed and enjoyed it throughout the meal. Seashells were also used as dishes, and you could feel the care put into even the smallest detail.​The six types of aged raw fish had a really plump and savory texture, filling my mouth with umami. ​When I ate it with the kelp salt and barley miso that came with it, the subtle sweetness and salty flavor were added, making it even more delicious. The sea bream shio ramen was perfect until the last course, with the flavor of sea bream subtly ingrained in the clear and light soup.

It's an izakaya that has the perfect atmosphere, taste, and value for money.
In particular, I was very satisfied because the course menu was comprehensive and all the menu items were delicious.

As the course is personally presented by a seafood sommelier, it has excellent freshness and flavor. The flow from appetizers to aged raw fish, grilled fish, and ramen was excellent. One table setting consists of appetizers that are almost too pretty to eat, and the aged raw fish is fresh and tasty.

The sauce for the shrimp ankage was rich and flavorful, and the ramen made with sea bream had a refreshing and clean broth that was as good as those at ramen restaurants. I think it would be great for hangovers too!

The seafood salad and grilled fish that I tried for the first time were both excellent in taste and texture, and the atmosphere was cozy, making it great for quiet conversation. It's also a perfect place for a meeting with friends or a date.

The staff were friendly, and the chef explained each course in detail, making the meal even more enjoyable.
This is a place I definitely want to visit again next time!

We had a multi-course family meal at the lunch room. I've been to several Chinese restaurants, but this is the first place where both the taste and service were the worst. The server seemed to be new to the workforce, but he had no service training at all. He had three rings on his fingers, gel nails with a neutral color on his fingernails, and a giblet band on his wrist while serving the food. He had an attitude of getting his work done quickly rather than being considerate of the customers, whether they were eating or not.
The first dish was abalone appetizer. Below, there was cold jellyfish and abalone, and the spicy mustard scent and sour cold vegetable tasted like eating raw konjac.
The second dish was somchai meatball soup, but it smelled sour and rotten that it would have been better not to have served it. It was so difficult to eat that I left it. It tasted like eating Korean soup after putting it in a food container and letting it sit for a long time. It had all kinds of flavors beyond sourness, but it was a fermented soup.
The third dish, Beijing Eight Jin Shark Fin, had a lot of shark fin in it. I had to find the shark fin as if I was playing a treasure hunt game.
The fourth dish, king prawns in orange cream sauce, was the most delicious of all the dishes. To be honest, I think it would be a big deal if the fried food wasn't tasty. The sauce was sweet and went well with the fruit.
The fifth dish, beef nanjawanse, came with a chunk of hamburger steak suitable for the number of people, but it was like a mini version of Ottogi's hamburger steak, and was just a chunk of meat that was rough and dry. It was really difficult to eat. The sauce didn't go well with the food and it wasn't delicious.
The sixth dish was a choice between Jjajangmyeon and stir-fried pot rice. Jjajangmyeon was more delicious. The fried pot rice had a bland taste of rice and leftovers roughly stir-fried in oil.
The seventh dish was yeonsishimiro. It was just a piece of red persimmon with a refreshing taste.
It was really unpleasant and unpleasant service. It's so bad I don't think I'll go anywhere near this place.

I visited around 6:30 on a weekday evening and waited about 15 minutes.
Two people ordered red pepper sweet and sour pork (large) and black bean noodles.

Red pepper sweet and sour pork — It is more appropriate to call it nurungji sweet and sour pork. It has a unique flavor thanks to the generous amount of crispy fried nurungji. The fried meat wasn't that crispy, but the combination of sauce and scorched rice was great.

Jjajangmyeon — It’s not particularly original, but it’s overall delicious and clean. The seasoning wasn't too overpowering, so it was easy to eat. There seemed to be more customers ordering Jjajang than Jjamppong.

The food comes out very quickly, and there are many regular customers who enjoy fine cuisine and Kaoliang liquor during dinner time. This restaurant has a reason why it has been loved by the local community for a long time.

Because it was busy and small, the staff wasn't very friendly, but the overall impression wasn't bad because there was a friendly owner.

This is a good upscale Chinese restaurant that I would like to come to with my parents if I get the chance.

Despite this, the taste and quality are maintained, but perhaps because of the influx of customers, long-time regulars find it difficult to settle down, and new visitors sometimes feel disappointed because they do not understand the culture of the existing store.

We mainly eat the restaurant's signature(?) menu items, nanjawansu and red pepper sweet and sour pork, along with black bean paste and jjamppong served in small portions.
If you want to add something special, I recommend the crab meat seafood dish. However, unlike typical neighborhood Chinese restaurants, it is a bit pricey.

If you want to visit this place, I recommend making a reservation these days.

reviews.text:
The crispy fried yakdol sweet and sour pork had chewy and light meat that went well with the sweet sauce.
The red pepper yuringi topped with Cheongyang peppers was a dish I kept coming back to as the refreshing sauce and crispy fries harmonized well.
I was particularly impressed by the spicyness of the peppers that cut through the greasiness.
Jjajangmyeon had a rich chunjang flavor and the noodles were chewy, so it was faithful to the basics.
This is a Chinese restaurant with ample portions overall, making it a good place to share several dishes.
I thought it was a good place to enjoy the atmosphere and taste in Apgujeong.

reviews.author: Stella Kim
reviews.text:
The truffle steak jjajangmyeon was really impressive. It was rich in flavor due to the generous amount of truffle, and it was a dish that made you feel good the whole time you ate it. The steak was of excellent quality, so you could clearly feel the flavor of the meat in every bite, and even the fried egg was done to perfection, so the overall balance was very good.

The macaron menbosha also exceeded expectations. The bread was made thin and not too thick, so the texture and taste of the shrimp was preserved. It was crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, so I could feel the harmony of the ingredients. I got the impression that it was a carefully prepared menu.

Uiseong Garlic Yuringi was unique starting from the scent of the minced garlic. The garlic flavor was deep and clean, while the meat was soft and luxurious. It was an impressive dish without being too spicy.

Overall, the menu composition was good, and the staff responded kindly, so I was able to eat comfortably. This is a place I would like to visit again.

reviews.author: Chanho Andrew Kim (MUYO)
reviews.text: After traveling here and there since my first visit, I visited for the first time in almost ten years. Dim sum seems to be almost the same as before, and I was glad that the menu was added to the menu. I mainly ate dim sum. 1) First of all, it was chewy without spreading blood. 2) Dim sum was big enough to be difficult to fit in one bite. 3) The filling had a fresh taste without any unpleasant smell. I thought it was a long-established restaurant(?) with age and tradition, and it was like fried radish rice cake, which I hated in Hong Kong because of its bad texture. I enjoyed the stir-fried radish rice cake because it had a chewy potato rice cake texture. For my meal, I ate Darurimyeon, which had the texture of Jjajangmyeon but was impressive with a milder taste. It is now a well-established restaurant among dim sum restaurants, and after wandering around many places, I am convinced that it is one of the best dim sum restaurants in Seoul.

reviews.author: Delirain Lee
reviews.text:
Two people searched for a dim sum restaurant and visited to celebrate a birthday.
It was a weekday evening, but I made a reservation because it was the end of the year.
I was able to make a reservation in advance through Catch Table. At Catch Table, you can make a reservation by paying a reservation deposit, or by registering Catch Pay, you can make a reservation without a reservation deposit.

There are Chinese menus, but the dim sum menu was the most popular.
Since there were two of us, we couldn't order very much food.

After mulling over the dim sum menu, I ordered shrimp dim sum with xiao long bao and chives (gu chaekyo).
In addition, I considered shrimp dim sum (he gau) and mushroom and pork (xiao mai), but I skipped it because there were other menu items.
The dim sum, Xiao Long Bao, was the most delicious and I recommend it.
Gu Chaekyo is pretty good.

As for other foods
I also ordered the recommended menu of fried shrimp wrapped in spring rolls.
Radish tteokbokkeum (radish tteokbokkeum) is as unique as it is said to be, with the taste of radish and the texture of rice cake.
It was unique and delicious, with a savory taste that felt like roasted potatoes.
I understand why it’s a popular menu item.

Among the dishes, I ordered kwaebarou. It had a strong vinegar taste, and this was also delicious.

Overall, the recommended menu items were delicious and recommended.

Pickles were served along with the dish so we could eat them together.
It would be nice to have drinks or beer together.

The set menu seems to be good in terms of composition and price. Next time I visit, I will order the set menu.

The price of dim sum is close to 10,000 won, and along with the dishes, it is expected to cost 40,000-50,000 won per person.

I plan to try the signature fried rice next time as it comes highly recommended.

reviews.author: tokomon 02 (tokomon)
reviews.text:
Review of what I bought with my own money-

1. Price: Geumeogyo 1.8 Garlic back rib dim sum 0.85 Guchaegyo 0.98 Shomai 0.98 Donggeureo 0.98 Signature fried rice 1.5 Add shrimp 0.2 Darumyeon 1.3 Gongcheongcheonghyangdaehongpo 0.8 Soryongpo 0.98 Jjim gyoza 0.89

2. Taste
- Geumeo Bridge is visually cute and pretty, but it’s not worth paying 20,000 won for.
- Garlic Back Ribs Dim Sum: So So
- Gu Chae-gyo: The chive flavor has its own opinion, but it is subtle and delicious.
- I recommend the round one rather than the Shomai one.
- The fried rice was delicious because each grain of rice was well-fried, but it had no impact and was just okay.
- Dealing: A unique taste that you won't get anywhere else. It's definitely not boring, but it's clean and there's nothing left in your mouth after you finish it. Instead, the surrounding vegetables absorb all the sauce, so it's salty haha.
-Gongcheongcheonghyangdaehongpo: It was a good tea for refreshing the mouth, but the tea was getting cold, so I asked for warm water separately and kept drinking more.
- Soryongpo Good
- Jijim Gyoza: I ate it and didn’t touch it, and my partner who went with me commented that it was covered in oil and didn’t feel particularly delicious.
​
3. Burial
The store is not that small and the servers are very friendly. I felt like they really provided attentive service. I wonder why there is a picture of a butt in the interior haha.
​
4. Accessibility
​I visited by public transportation and on foot. The alleys in Apgujeong were narrow to begin with, but cars were squeezing in so I had to look carefully when visiting by car.

5. Intention to revisit
​None. It's not that the dim sum itself wasn't delicious, but because it's Apgujeong, the prices are very high, and there are restaurants of a similar level and much cheaper, so I don't think I'll go there again.  Had a good experience.

One-line review: A place worth visiting at least once to take Instagram-worthy photos of goldfish dim sum or when you want to eat expensive food in a stylish atmosphere using someone else's money rather than your own.

reviews.text: With spring just around the corner, I had lunch with a friend at the Apgujeong Rodeo Chinese restaurant. It is a modern Chinese restaurant run by a chef from Black and White Chef 2. It has an impressive open kitchen and emerald green interior, and also has a private room. I ordered cucumber salad, dongpo pork with buns, beef and sweet and sour pork, and mapo tofu, and each menu item stood out as a sophisticated reinterpretation of existing Chinese food. In particular, the dongpo pork that melted in your mouth, the sweet and sour pork with a buttery flavor, and the mapo tofu with a deep Mala flavor were all impressive. A place that offers a special gourmet experience by adding a modern sensibility to the charm of traditional Chinese food.

I went to Bobo Restaurant, a Chinese restaurant in Apgujeong run by chef Jang Bo-won, who appeared in Black and White Chef 2. I had high expectations because it was a modern take on traditional Chinese Chinese food that had been passed down for three generations, but I was impressed by the deep spiciness of the homemade red pepper oil and the meticulous cooking.

The cool and spicy oyster jjamppong with plenty of oysters, the crispy and moist dried monkfish, and the rich Mala-flavored mapo tofu were all satisfying.

There was a private room, so it was a good place for gatherings or dates, and we finished the meal specially with red pepper oil ice cream.

We highly recommend this Apgujeong Chinese restaurant with a different dimension, complete with the deep spiciness of homemade red pepper oil!!! It was really delicious! This is a restaurant I want to go to again. 😍

reviews.author: Hong Soon-eon
reviews.text:
I think this is the best dumpling soup restaurant in South Korea. This house’s dumplings raised me. It’s a taste I’ve had since I was in high school, so for nearly 50 years. This is a house that continues from the dumplings that the grandmother in the frame made.

The filling of the dumplings is bean sprouts, well-squeezed tofu, a little bit of pork, and pepper. It is simple and not excessive. Since our family is from Gaeseong, we also make dumplings, but despite this, our dumplings feel like a ‘standard’. The dumpling skin is moderately thick and chewy, and does not disintegrate even when added to the soup.

The soup is also impressive. The base is a clear meat broth, and if you add seasoning (aka dadaegi) according to your taste, it becomes spicy. It's also great as a hangover. Bean curd is a must-try menu item. You can see the texture of North Korean food.

The attention to detail of this house can also be felt in the service that provides warm water in the winter. Another surprising thing is that they always make their own dumplings by renting a separate store space next door. Knowing how expensive rent would be in Apgujeong-dong, the fact that they chose ‘homemade dumplings’ over efficiency makes this restaurant more trustworthy.

During my military training camp in 1990, when asked what I wanted to eat most when I was on vacation, someone mentioned this house. It's amazing that you can still eat dumplings like that. I hope it stays for a long time.

First, dumpling soup is filled with dumplings in a clean, cool soup. It was not spicy and light, so the spoon kept going. But there was something else that really impressed me: red pepper pancake and mung bean pancake!

The red pepper pancake had a rich filling and a savory egg coating, giving it a richer flavor the more you chewed it, while the mung bean pancake was crispy yet moist on the inside, giving it a truly authentic taste. To be honest, the pancake was more memorable than the “Dumpling House” sign.

The store received a message saying, “We’re sorry. We will be careful,” and Catchtable said, “The store is claiming infringement of rights and requesting that the posting be taken down.”

The review I left on Catchtable has been suspended, so I will leave a review on Google with the same content.

I don't understand what part of the store's rights was violated, so I'd like to ask the store.

Are you uncomfortable with the fact that the food is not that good? So, isn't it our business to think about ways to improve how to make food taste good to the public? If I delete a review that says the food wasn't that good, does bad food become delicious?
Should I write about tasteless food as delicious?

I left a review to share the feelings and experiences that I and my friends felt, and I left a review of the places I visited because I thought it would be helpful to other people in choosing a restaurant.
This is because I also refer to other people's reviews when making choices, whether it's restaurants, shopping, or travel. Doesn't everyone do that? The decision is up to the consumer.

Do you want to keep the restaurant as a perfect 5-star restaurant by leaving only the 5-star reviews you want and reporting and taking down all the reviews that are not?

We believe that service evolves through continuous improvement, education, and customer experience. I left a review saying the atmosphere was good, but looking at the store's current attitude, it seems like the only thing that matters is how it looks.

If I violate the store's rights, can I report the store for violating the user's rights to leave a review of the consumer's experience and share personal information with others?
It's very unpleasant and I wonder if this is the right treatment for a restaurant that paid 260,000 won for 1 hour and 30 minutes.

I am writing a detailed review of this new Italian restaurant. I've been frequenting New York for the past 10 years and have tried many famous pizzerias, from Italy to Tokyo to New York. Think of places like Savoy in Tokyo or Lukali in New York. This restaurant may not be compared to the world's most prestigious pizza places, but it is by far the best in Korea. It feels like a miniature version of the legendary American pizzeria ‘Mother Wolf’.

To be honest, it is no exaggeration to say that this pizza place is currently the best pizza place in Korea. That's because they use proper pizza ovens like those used in Tokyo and Italy. There are probably no pizza restaurants in Korea that use this type of oven.

The pizza is Tokyo-style Neapolitan, and the pasta, like carbonara, is cooked to al dente perfection in a proper oven and boasts great taste. The chef's service is also excellent. During lunch hours, free drinks and salads are provided. Plus, in this day and age of high prices, the prices are very reasonable.

Most Italian restaurants in Korea have similar tastes, but this one boasts a truly unique and authentic taste. The atmosphere is really nice too.

This place is truly underrated, I hope it becomes a huge success in the future!

reviews.text: When I went on a Saturday, they said they only take reservations on weekends, so I came back and was curious about why I came, so I made a reservation and went an hour later. reviews.text:
I visited 10 minutes before opening time on a weekend and there were about 3-4 teams in front. Because I made a reservation on Naver in advance, I was able to sit in my reserved seat right away.
(✅️Reservations are recommended when visiting)
I ordered Texas sous vide beef rib pizza and mozzarella caprese and the sous vide meat was so delicious. The manager cuts the meat himself and puts it on the pizza. Ordering one drink or one alcoholic beverage per person is required, and there are a variety of beers available, so it would be a good place to have a beer. There are also a variety of non-alcoholic beverages.
Since it is a downtown restaurant, it felt crowded and cluttered... but it's like this everywhere you go haha.
This is a special food that is hard to taste, so if you like sous vide and pizza, please visit.

reviews.author: RY C
reviews.text:
I went there because I was really curious about Woodae Galbi Pizza.
It was fun to watch the performance of putting meat directly on top of the pizza, and the meat was very tender.
It was a little greasy, but it seemed appropriate because of the jalapenos, and the pizza had a crispy finish, so it was delicious.

The carbonara was more delicious than I expected. I think it was more savory thanks to the yolk!

Since it is a pub, one alcoholic beverage per person is required.
I tried beer, rose wine, and Earl Gray highball.
Rosé wine has a very strong acidity, so it is not recommended for those who do not like acidity very much! The Earl Gray Highball didn't feel like it was very delicious either. The beer (lager) was the most plain and clean, so it went well with it.

reviews.author: Jihye Kim
reviews.text: Sous vide steak Detroit pizza (34,000 won) was very delicious. The thick, fluffy and airy dough was excellent, and the sous vide steak as a topping had a soft yet chewy texture that was fantastic. There are many reviews saying the wait is long, but perhaps because I visited on a weekday, there was no wait at all. If you're worried, it would be a good idea to make a reservation on Naver in advance before visiting. Naver reservations can be made up to one day in advance.

I had dinner at Abeq Cheongdam, and overall I was very satisfied with the food, service, and atmosphere.
The food, from the main menu to the sides, was not overly seasoned and the ingredients were well-flavored. In particular, the pasta and meat dishes had a good texture and sauce balance, so I was able to eat them all without getting tired of them.

From the moment you step inside, the space feels special. Artistic objects placed throughout the restaurant create a refined, stylish atmosphere—it’s not just a meal, but a true dining experience.
Every dish exceeded expectations.
The avocado shrimp salad was beautifully balanced, with fresh herbal notes and a soft, smooth texture.
The uni pasta was rich and creamy, carrying a clean ocean aroma that felt incredibly fresh.
The sim katsu was cooked to perfection, with deep, savory flavors that paired wonderfully with the sauce.
And the absolute highlight: the gnocchi.
Perfectly chewy with a silky, well-balanced sauce—never too heavy, yet full of flavor. It was easily the best dish of the night.
To top it off, the service was exceptional.
The staff were warm, professional, and truly kind—even the valet was incredibly courteous.
Amazing food, beautiful space, flawless service.
If 5 stars is the maximum, this place truly deserves 10.

reviews.author: YJ Oh
reviews.text: A high-end Italian restaurant located in Apgujeong-dong or Sinsa-dong in the administrative district. The sign at the entrance is so small that first-time visitors may get a little lost. The store is not large, but the high ceilings give it a comfortable feel, and the interior is luxurious. It is said that there are two internal floors above the kitchen and about three private rooms. There is a large wine cellar inside the store, and many types of wine are on display inside. Looking at the wine list, like an Italian restaurant, it mainly consists of Italian wines. It feels like the food is neatly served in small amounts on a large plate. The taste of the food, including pasta, is top-notch. As a luxury restaurant, the prices are high. The staff are polite and very friendly. There is a parking space in front and next to the store, and only valet parking is available.

reviews.author: J Lim (James)
reviews.text:
(Meal at the end of October 24)
At Mongone, I watched some related videos and liked the blog reviews, so I tried the lunch course with my wife.
At first, when I heard that the lunch course was 79,000 won, it was much cheaper than the Choi Dot I visited last time, so I went there out of curiosity and half anticipation.  Moreover, it is also a certified pasta restaurant (especially Vongole).
In conclusion, I feel like this course was just in this price range.

The good thing is that the seasoning was good, not too salty or bland.
The bikini sandwich was fun and delicious.
I additionally ordered veal tenderloin, and it was tender and delicious.
Tiramisu and vanilla ice cream were also good.

The most disappointing thing was the pasta, which was called the signature dish, and even though it was imported directly from Italy, it was clearly different from fresh noodles.
I was very disappointed with the texture of the tortellini and spaghetti vongole. The signature vongole had more of a spicy flavor than a garlic flavor, but I personally found the oily feeling too much. My wife liked the stone octopus steak, but it was a bit tough for me.
The tableware also left a lot to be desired.
Although the lunch boasts of using ingredients directly delivered from local Italian sources, it actually leaves a lot to be desired.

reviews.author: Ho Jung Lee
reviews.text: This is an Italian restaurant located next to Hanyang Town on Apgujeong Rodeo Street. It allows you to enjoy the taste of ingredients sourced from mainland Italy. The pre-dinner dishes allow you to really taste the flavor of each ingredient. The main dishes are tenderloin and lamb ribs. The tenderloin is extremely soft and the lamb ribs are well-cooked so that you can only smell the lamb without any smell. The atmosphere of the store is cozy and has a European feel. All the staff, including the manager, are friendly, so you can start and end your meal in a pleasant mood. A detailed explanation of the dish is provided for each course menu, so you can understand and eat the dish and ingredients.
